conditions: The source scope target must convert to a Python PROP.
The source operator must be NEGATION with operator NOT.
operatorMappings.reason: Both implementations define truth-functional proposition negation; scope is represented by the nested argument.
Unknown polarity is not logical negation and must not be represented as NOT.

conditions: Source force must explicitly identify epistemic possibility (for example epistemic_possibility).
The scoped target must convert to PROP.
operatorMappings.reason: The Python modal signature distinguishes force and flavor; the source operator label alone does not establish both.

conditions: Source force must explicitly identify epistemic possibility.
The scoped target must convert to PROP.
operatorMappings.reason: MIGHT can express epistemic possibility in the Workbench source parser, but the mapping is gated by explicit force metadata.

conditions: Source force must explicitly identify epistemic possibility.
The scoped target must convert to PROP.
operatorMappings.reason: MAY is mapped only when the source explicitly resolves it as epistemic possibility, not permission.

conditions: Source force must explicitly identify epistemic necessity.
The scoped target must convert to PROP.
operatorMappings.reason: NECESSARY is not enough by itself to distinguish epistemic, deontic, dynamic, or circumstantial necessity.

conditions: Source force must explicitly identify deontic obligation.
The scoped target must convert to PROP.
operatorMappings.reason: The Python kernel can represent deontic necessity, but the source force must explicitly support that reading.

conditions: Source force must explicitly identify deontic modality.
The scoped target must convert to PROP.
operatorMappings.reason: SHOULD is not mapped from its surface label alone; explicit deontic force is required.

conditions: A source-side resolver must disambiguate epistemic necessity from obligation or other readings.
operatorMappings.reason: The Workbench source parser explicitly marks MUST as necessity-or-obligation ambiguous.

conditions: A source-side resolver must disambiguate possibility from ability.
operatorMappings.reason: The Workbench source parser marks COULD as possible_or_ability; no unique Python flavor follows.

conditions: A source-side resolver must disambiguate ability from permission or circumstantial possibility.
operatorMappings.reason: The Workbench source parser marks CAN as ability_or_permission.

conditions: Resolve the modal flavor before conversion.
operatorMappings.reason: The source explicitly preserves a disjunction of modal readings.
The Python MODAL operator has no expectation force; expectation must not be recast as epistemic possibility or necessity.

conditions: Source force must be temporal_future and the source use must be future tense rather than volition or prediction.
The scoped target must convert to PROP.
operatorMappings.reason: The Workbench parser classifies WILL as asserted with temporal_future force; convert it to TENSE only when that explicit analysis is retained.

conditions: Resolve conditional, hypothetical, habitual, or volitional reading.
operatorMappings.reason: WOULD is not one stable modal force and must not be mapped to a generic Python modal.
An unresolved quantifier scope is not a quantified proposition; preserve it as unresolved metadata.

conditions: A valid restrictor expression and bound variable must be present.
Every bound occurrence must be linked to the same variable and restrictor.
The Python restrictor and scope must each be PROP.
quantifierMappings.reason: Workbench's explicit variableBinding can be represented by Python Q when the bound-variable structure is complete.

conditions: A valid restrictor expression and bound variable must be present.
Every bound occurrence must be linked to the same variable and restrictor.
quantifierMappings.reason: The Python Q operator supports EXISTS; Workbench's current semantic-core quantifier set does not directly enumerate EXISTS in all authoring paths, so accept only explicit source nodes.

conditions: A valid restrictor and bound variable must be present.
The count must be exactly one.
quantifierMappings.reason: The target kernel supports EXACTLY with integer n.

conditions: A valid restrictor and bound variable must be present.
quantifierMappings.reason: The target kernel supports AT_LEAST with integer n.

conditions: A valid restrictor and bound variable must be present.
quantifierMappings.reason: The target kernel supports AT_MOST with integer n.

conditions: Source semantics must be the Workbench NO form: universal quantification over a negated body.
The restrictor and bound-variable links must be valid.
quantifierMappings.reason: Workbench represents NO as FORALL over NOT(body); preserve that actual structure instead of substituting a different quantifier.

conditions: Negation must scope over the completed universal expression, not inside its restrictor or body.
quantifierMappings.reason: The outer NOT is semantically distinct from NO and must remain outside Q.
Unknown or missing quantifier values cannot be guessed.

conditions: All operands must convert to PROP.
Operand identity and all operands must be preserved.
connectiveMappings.reason: Both systems support conjunction over propositions.

conditions: All operands must convert to PROP.
Preserve inclusive_or_unspecified; do not infer exclusive-or.
connectiveMappings.reason: Both systems support disjunction over propositions; Workbench's unspecified disjunction remains inclusive-or-unspecified.

conditions: Explicit antecedentId and consequentId must be present.
logicalStatus must be conditional_not_asserted.
Both clauses must convert to PROP.
connectiveMappings.reason: Python COND represents a natural-language conditional and is distinct from material IMPLIES.

conditions: marker must be unless.
antecedentInterpretation must equal negated_exception_condition_equivalent_to_if_not_P_then_Q.
The antecedent graph must already contain explicit NOT(P).
logicalStatus must be exception_relation_asserted.
Both clauses must convert to PROP.
connectiveMappings.reason: The Workbench graph already negates the unless antecedent. Convert that explicit NOT(P) and the consequent to COND without adding or removing negation.

conditions: A separate temporal-clause interpretation is required.
connectiveMappings.reason: A temporal when-clause is not interchangeable with an ordinary conditional; the Python kernel has temporal relations but no direct clause-attachment operator.
No exact concessive connective exists in the Python expression grammar.
No exact contrast connective exists in the Python expression grammar.

scopePolicy.representation: Workbench stores scope as explicit graph references (scope.targetId, antecedentId, consequentId, operandIds); Python stores scope compositionally as nested Node arguments.
requirements: Convert the complete target subtree before constructing its parent operator.
Preserve exact nesting order; NOT(MODAL(P)) is not MODAL(NOT(P)).
Preserve connective operand order and directed antecedent/consequent roles.
Detect missing targets, cycles, multiply-referenced nodes, and disconnected expression nodes; do not silently omit them.
Only map a source scopeKind when its target relation is structurally equivalent; descriptive labels alone do not change operator scope.
Return PARTIAL or UNSUPPORTED when a child cannot be represented; do not build a misleading complete parent.

policy.unknownBehavior: Unknown operators, forces, quantifiers, and connectives remain explicitly unresolved or unsupported.
policy.lossBehavior: Never drop, flatten, invert, or reorder scope; never reinterpret UNKNOWN as NOT; never conflate COND with material IMPLIES.
policy.versioning: Published registry versions are immutable. Changes require a new version, source evidence, and automated conformance tests.
